newsitem.title: JAPAN: Green Cross, Yoshitomi fall on merger announcement.
newsitem.headline: Green Cross, Yoshitomi fall on merger announcement.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market on Tuesday gave a thumbs down to the planned takeover of scandal-tainted drug company Green Cross Corp by another Japanese pharmaceuticals firm.
Green Cross shares slid 54 yen to 512 yen as of 0406 GMT following Monday's announcement that the drug maker will be taken over by Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd.

Green Cross became the second-biggest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Shares in Yoshitomi also fell 49 yen to 841 yen. It was also among the five biggest losers in percentage terms in the section.

Under the merger deal, five shares of Green Cross will be exchanged for three Yoshitomi shares. Green Cross, hurt by a scandal involving HIV-tainted blood products, will be dissolved on the planned merger on October 1, the companies said.
Traders attributed the drop in Green Cross shares to an adjustment prompted by the ratio of the merger.
Based on Monday's closing prices, each Green Cross share would be worth 534 yen, compared with its actual close of 566 yen.
Beyond these technical factors, the future of the two companies also remains cloudy, analysts said.
Ritsuo Watanabe, an analyst at Kokusai Securities, said in a commentary that the two companies' shares may stay weak for the time being because of limited benefits from the merger.

The merged firm is expected to be the 10th-largest on the first section of the Tokyo exchange with sales of 150 billion yen in the year to March 1998. But this would not be enough to compete equally with big domestic and foreign rivals, he said.
"As far as Yoshitomi is concerned, the firm is rescuing Green Cross and some investors don't like the idea of the added financial burden," said a trader at a Japanese second-tier brokerage.
Green Cross has been at the centre of a scandal concerning HIV-tainted blood products after former presidents of the firm were indicted last October on charges of professional negligence.

It faces compensation payments of some 24 billion yen to people infected with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, through use of its blood products. The products were not heat-treated even though company documents showed that officials knew there was a risk such unheated products could be infected with HIV.
The new company to be created on the merger will take over responsibility for compensation to victims of the tainted blood products, the two companies said.

Toshihide Yuda, an analyst at ING Barings in Tokyo, said the planned merger contained high risks given uncertainty over Green Cross's compensation problems. He assigned a sell rating on both Green Cross and Yoshitomi.

The new company could face additional compensation payments of up to 100 billion yen if all victims were to sue Green Cross, and the merged company might not have sufficient funds to cope with the potential need for such added compensation payments, Yuda said in a commentary on Tuesday.
Yuda said Green Cross at present has funds of 23 billion yen and Yoshitomi has funds of 24 billion yen. -- Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9404
